text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* After four years and a two-day fight with European partners in Brussels, the lira was allowed to re-enter the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM) at a central parity of 990 lire to the mark. The lira will have to observe the 15 percent fluctuation bands within the ERM (all).
* Prime Minister Romano Prodi says the parity is realistic and reflects the competitiveness of the Italian economy, adding he is "not 100 percent, but 99 percent" satisfied (all).
* Opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi says "this is not a favourable level, the Italian industry deserved a higher parity" meaning a rate in the 1,000s (all).

* Parties supporting the government in parliament are split after leftist PDS leader Massimo D'Alema said light drugs should be legalized: deputy prime minister Walter Veltroni says "the government has not discussed this issue" (Repubblica).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
